env.description: Env lists variable names whose values are part of the cache key.

CacheConfig.description: CacheConfig is the [cache] section for --cache result reuse.

enabled.description: Enabled turns the hook off when false (it then never rewrites).

default_rules.description: DefaultRules appends the built-in rules after the user's (default true).

permission.description:
Permission is "" (the rewritten command goes through Claude Code's
normal permission flow) or "allow" (auto-approve rewritten commands).

max_wait.description: MaxWait is passed as --max-wait and added to the Bash tool timeout.

binary.description:
Binary is how the rewritten command calls heavyq ("" = "heavyq" when it
is on PATH, else the absolute path of the running binary).

HookConfig.description: HookConfig is the [hook] section: how `heavyq hook claude-pretooluse` rewrites agent commands.

HookRule.description: HookRule wraps commands whose words start with one of Match.

legacy_lock_files.description:
Local only: lock files shared with legacy `flock <file> cmd` users.
When set they replace the generated heavy slot files.

transport.description: argv prefix; the remote script is appended as ONE argument

work_dir.description: remote dir holding git/, wt/, slots/, cache/

git_url.description: where bare repos live, as seen by `git push`

cache_hook.description: shell snippet run in the worktree before the command

env_path.description: directories put first on the remote command's PATH ("~/" = remote home)

MachineConfig.description: MachineConfig describes the local machine or one remote.

holdout_pct.description:
HoldoutPct is the share of eligible events logged but not shown, 0-100
(default 20). 100 is shadow mode: events are logged and measured, the
agent sees nothing.

auto_mute.description: AutoMute silences a rule that shows too little lift (default true).

min_events.description:
MinEvents is how many resolved events each arm needs before the lift
is judged (default 200).

min_lift_pp.description:
MinLiftPP is the lift, in percentage points, below which a rule is
muted (default 10).

MentorConfig.description: MentorConfig is the [mentor] section: the experiment behind `heavyq hook claude-posttooluse` (docs/mentor.md).

remote.description: "local" (the default), "auto" (the scheduler picks among local and the configured remotes, free slots first) or the name of a [[remote]]. A gate with its own remote key keeps it; --remote wins over both.

ProofConfig.description: Where `heavyq item done --run` and `heavyq gate run` run proofs. The same table in a repository's heavyq.toml overrides it there.

poll.description: Poll is the delay between two scheduling attempts of a waiting ticket.

force_after.description:
ForceAfter: a head-of-line ticket with one candidate machine waiting
longer than this skips the load check (anti-starvation). It still needs
a free slot and the RAM for its job.

resource_gate.description: ResourceGate disables RAM/load checks when false (slots only).

auto.description: Auto enables score-based placement for tickets without --remote.

load_weight_mb.description: LoadWeightMB is k in score = free_mb - k * load1.

remote_down_max.description:
RemoteDownMax: a remote-only ticket exits 76 after its remotes have been
unreachable this long.

hold_for.description:
HoldFor: a freshly claimed job reserves its RAM budget for this long,
because a starting job has not grown yet.

probe_timeout.description: ProbeTimeout bounds one remote metrics probe.

need_gh_repos.description: Repository directory names whose commands call the GitHub CLI with this machine's login: runs there behave as if --need-gh were given (this machine only).

name.description: Pool name; becomes part of the environment variable HEAVYQ_<NAME>.

values.description: A range "4100-4199", or a list of names or integers.

size.description: A capacity-only pool: the values are 1..size.

port.description: true: the values are TCP ports, probed before they are handed out. Absent: a pool called "port" or ending in "_port" is a port pool.

Pool.description: A named pool of values handed out with --needs: ports, database names, browser seats.

pool.description:
PoolSpecs are the [[pool]] tables as written; normalize validates them
into Pools. A pool of the same name in heavyq.toml replaces the user's.

title: heavyq user config
description: heavyq's user configuration, ~/.config/heavyq/config.toml: slots, RAM budgets, remotes, hook rules, cache and pools. Every key is optional.
